# `fda` checker rules, rule set 1

<!-- Generated: go test ./internal/bomscore -run TestFDARuleListDocument -update. Do not edit. -->

The checks of the profile `fda` of `rearm bomutils score`, in the order of the report. A JSON report names this list in the `ruleSetVersion` of its `fda` profile and the engine that ran in `engine`; a report whose `fda` profile has no `ruleSetVersion` was written by an engine older than rule set 1.

The number is the engine's and numbers this list only: a `ruleSetVersion` anywhere else than in the `fda` profile of an engine report is another number.

This list says what each check reads and when it passes, so that the checker can be compared with what you expect of it. It is not a statement that a document which passes meets the expectations of the source document.

The rule set number changes whenever this list changes in any way, and whenever a check is changed to decide differently on some document. The same number means the same list.

Source: FDA, "Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions", section V.A.4(b), 2026-02-03, https://www.fda.gov/media/119933/download

| Id | Title | Level | Scope | What it checks | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fda.baseline.author-name` | Author Name | REQUIRED | DOCUMENT | The document names an author: CycloneDX `metadata.authors[].name` or `metadata.manufacturer.name`; SPDX a `Person:` or `Organization:` creator. A tool, `metadata.supplier` and the deprecated `metadata.manufacture` are not an author. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Author Name |
| `fda.baseline.timestamp` | Timestamp | REQUIRED | DOCUMENT | The document has a creation timestamp, CycloneDX `metadata.timestamp` or SPDX `created`, in one of the timestamp forms below. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Timestamp |
| `fda.baseline.supplier-name` | Supplier Name | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every component names who made or supplies it: CycloneDX `manufacturer.name`, `supplier.name`, `authors[].name` or `author`; SPDX `supplier` or `originator`. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Supplier Name |
| `fda.baseline.component-name` | Component Name | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every component has a name. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Component Name |
| `fda.baseline.version-string` | Version String | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every component has a version. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Version String |
| `fda.baseline.component-hash` | Component Hash | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every component has a hash entry with both an algorithm and a value (CycloneDX `hashes[]`; SPDX `checksums[]`), or, in CycloneDX, a property `reliza:support:justifiedUnknown:hash` whose value is one of the reason codes below. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Component Hash |
| `fda.baseline.unique-identifier` | Unique Identifier | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every component has an identifier: CycloneDX `purl`, `cpe`, `swid.tagId`, `swhid[]` or `omniborId[]`; SPDX an external reference of type `purl`, `cpe22Type`, `cpe23Type`, `swh` or `gitoid`. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Unique Identifier |
| `fda.baseline.relationship` | Relationship | REQUIRED | DOCUMENT | Every described component declares its direct dependencies or states that it has none; what another component declares does not count. CycloneDX: a `dependencies[]` entry whose `ref` is the `bom-ref` of `metadata.component`, with a non-empty `dependsOn`; or a `compositions[]` entry with `aggregate` `complete` whose `dependencies[]` lists that `bom-ref`. SPDX, for each described package: `DEPENDS_ON` or `CONTAINS` from it to a package of the document or to `NONE`; or the mirrors, `DEPENDENCY_OF` or `CONTAINED_BY` from a package of the document or from `NONE` to it. Any other end (a file, `NOASSERTION`, another document, an unknown id) does not count. The check fails when nothing is described: CycloneDX without `metadata.component` or without its `bom-ref`; SPDX without a `DESCRIBES` relationship from the document to one of its packages, or `DESCRIBED_BY` the other way. | V.A.4(b); NTIA Framing 2nd ed. 2.2, Relationship |
| `fda.component.support-level` | Software level of support | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every judged component has a property `reliza:support:levelOfSupport` whose value is one of the level-of-support values below; one such property is enough, whatever another of that name says. Which components are judged is said below. SPDX 2.x has no place for the level of support: every package fails and none is skipped. | V.A.4(b) |
| `fda.component.end-of-support` | End-of-support date | REQUIRED | COMPONENT | Every judged component has an end-of-support date: CycloneDX a property `cdx:lifecycle:milestone:endOfSupport`, SPDX 2.3 `validUntilDate`, whose value is in one of the end-of-support date forms below; or, in CycloneDX, a property `reliza:support:justifiedUnknown:endOfSupport` whose value is one of the reason codes below. One such property is enough, whatever another of that name says. Which components are judged is said below. SPDX 2.1 and 2.2 have no place for the date: every package fails and none is skipped. | V.A.4(b) |
| `fda.document.vulnerabilities` | Known vulnerabilities and their assessment | INFO | DOCUMENT | Nothing is read: known vulnerabilities and their assessment are delivered as VDR/VEX with the submission, not in the SBOM. Always NOT_ASSESSED. | V.A.4(b) |

- A `DOCUMENT` check passes or fails on the document. A `COMPONENT` check passes when it judges at least one component and every component it judges has what the check asks for or, where the check takes one, a justification. With no component to judge it fails, at `0/0`: every `COMPONENT` check of a document without components, and the two support checks, with the note `no supportable component`, when they judge none of the components there are.
- Level `REQUIRED`: a failing check makes the verdict `NOT_READY`, whatever the other checks say; with none failing, a check that could not be evaluated (`ERROR`) makes it `UNKNOWN`; with neither, the verdict is `READY`. Level `INFO`: reported, never changes the verdict.
- A component is every component of the document except the described one: CycloneDX every entry of `components[]`, nested ones included, but not `metadata.component` nor the components nested in it; SPDX every package the document does not describe. With `--skip-files`, file components (CycloneDX type `file`; SPDX 2.3 `primaryPackagePurpose` `FILE`) are left out of every `COMPONENT` check as well, and the report says so in `options.skipFiles`.
- A name, version, author, producer, identifier, hash algorithm or hash value counts as missing when, blanks around it ignored, it is empty or is exactly `NOASSERTION` or `NONE`, in upper case.
- The level-of-support values, the reason codes, the value `true` of `reliza:support:selfComponent`, the component types and the property names are matched exactly: no trimming, no case folding.
- Timestamp forms. The value, blanks around it ignored, is read by Go's `time.Parse` with the layout `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00`; that is close to RFC 3339 and not the same. Accepted, for example: `2026-10-01T12:00:00Z`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00+02:00`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00.25Z`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00,25Z`. Refused, for example: `2026-10-01`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00`, `2026-10-01T12:00Z`, `2026-10-01 12:00:00Z`, `2026-10-01t12:00:00Z`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00z`, `2026-10-01T12:00:00+0200`, `2026-10-01T23:59:60Z`.
- End-of-support date forms. The value, blanks around it ignored, is read by Go's `time.Parse` with the layout `2006-01-02`, `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`. Accepted, for example: `2030-01-02`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05Z`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05+02:00`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05.5`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05,5Z`. Refused, for example: `20300102`, `2030-01`, `2030-02-30`, `2030-01-02T03:04`, `2030-01-02 03:04:05`, `2030-01-02t03:04:05`, `2030-01-02T03:04:05z`.
- Level-of-support values: `abandoned`, `actively maintained`, `no longer maintained`.
- A component the two support checks do not judge neither passes nor fails. In CycloneDX they do not judge a component whose `type` is one of `cryptographic-asset`, `data`, `device`, `file`, `machine-learning-model` (a component without a type is judged), nor a component with a property `reliza:support:selfComponent` of value `true`. In SPDX 2.3, `fda.component.end-of-support` does not judge a package whose `primaryPackagePurpose` is one of `DEVICE`, `FILE`.
- Reason codes, each valid on either property: `COMMUNITY_PROJECT`, `DISTRIBUTION_PUBLISHES_NO_HASH`, `NO_COMMITTED_END_OF_SUPPORT`, `OTHER`, `SUPPLIER_PUBLISHES_NO_DATE`, `VENDORED_SOURCE_NO_HASH`.
- An SPDX 2.x document is always `NOT_READY` under this profile: `fda.component.support-level` fails.
